title: ZWF07 7-round AES / aes-7r-id-general-zwf2007

target.description: 7 nonlinear AES rounds with the initial whitening addition and no final MixColumns. The recovered material is specified below.Endpoint: 112 mixed subkey bits: four bytes K0, eight bytes K7 and two bytes K6*.

success.description: The source gives partial-subkey outputs and expected wrong-candidate counts, not numerical end-to-end recovery success. In particular,2^-17 in Section4.1 and2^-18.5 in Section5 arise by multiplying expected survivors by outer guesses; they are not independently measured attack-failure probabilities. The local per-fixed-wrong-key model is preserved without assuming independent pairs beyond the source heuristic. Existing source arithmetic conflicts, if applicable, remain unchanged.

review.scope: Exact-edition targeted success audit of endpoint-specific probability, candidate retention and resource passages; not a new full-paper/forward audit. Local models and expected survivor counts remain separate from aggregate recovery.

components.description: Section4.2/5: eight ciphertext byte equalities in the relevant six/seven-round subroutine. For the eight-round extension this is after peeling the guessed eighth-round key, not a direct eight-round ciphertext sieve.
PDF9 footnote1: source approximate probability that the other eight differences are nonzero. Source complexity omits this near-one factor; no independence-based exact replacement is imposed.
PDF9 Section5 Step3(b): local three-byte sieve under the first four-byte K7 guess.
PDF9 Section5 Step3(c)i: additional three-byte sieve under the second four-byte K7 guess.
PDF6/9 Sections4.1/5: source4*2^-8 for one of four possible zero-byte patterns, conditional on the guessed terminal key.
Sections4.1–5: about2^10 entries in the32-bit input-difference bin out of2^32 whitening guesses. This source mean-elimination fraction is not a guarantee for each pair or key.
PDF7/10: source per-fixed-wrong32-bit whitening guess survival under the specified 2^28.5 eligible-pair model. Multiplying by guesses gives an expected survivor count, not an end-to-end probability.
